themes.theme: Kettlebell snatch test timer: five or ten minutes, and a cue to switch hands

Kettlebell Monster describes the common standards as 100 snatches in 5 minutes or 200 in 10, with a hand switch on a plan such as every full minute. Interval Timer's kettlebell page uses one minute of snatches and one minute of rest as pacing practice so the hands stay on the bell.

themes.theme: 30-15 intermittent fitness test timer: 30 seconds out, 15 seconds walking, faster every stage
themes.hook: A repeating 30/15 timer holds one speed. The 30-15 test speeds up every stage, and the beeps inside the 30 seconds are what set the pace.

Martin Buchheit describes the test as 30-second 40m shuttles with 15 seconds of walking, starting at 8 km/h and rising 0.5 km/h each stage. The beeps inside the 30 seconds are the pace, and one beep at the start does not tell me where I should be
The run ends on a double beep that is not always at a line, and I do not know which way to walk

themes.theme: Little method interval timer: 60 seconds hard and 75 seconds easy

themes.theme: Billat 30/30 interval timer: 30 seconds at vVO2max and 30 seconds at half of that pace
themes.hook: The Billat 30/30 is two equal halves, and how long you keep going comes from your time to exhaustion at that pace, not from eight Tabata rounds
themes.evidence: Reddit OAuth, xpoz, Google Search Console and Keyword Planner skipped (not available in this cloud environment); web search only. LW Coaching programs the Billat 30-30 as 30 seconds at 100% of vVO2max and 30 seconds at 50%, repeated until the work plus the recoveries add up to about two to two-and-a-half times your time to exhaustion at that pace. A 20/10 Tabata clock and a 30-seconds-on, four-minutes-easy sprint clock both run a different session.
pain_quotes: I started an eight-round timer because that is the preset, and the 30/30 ended before the pace was supposed to accumulate
The easy 30 seconds has to stay near half of vVO2max, and a full stop turns the next one into a fresh sprint
I cannot type a round count until I know how long I can hold the pace, so a fixed-round timer is a guess
themes.distinctFrom: Closest scored neighbour is best-tabata-timer at 0.13, which is 20 seconds on and 10 off for eight rounds. This answers Billat's 30/30: equal 30-second halves at vVO2max and at half of that pace, continued for about 2 to 2.5 times your time to exhaustion at vVO2max. gibala-sprint-interval-timer is 30 seconds all-out and about four minutes easy. themes.theme: Timmons protocol timer: 20 seconds flat-out, about two minutes easy, three efforts

themes.theme: Murph timer: two miles on one clock, and a middle you partition instead of an AMRAP
themes.hook: Murph is for time. Twenty rounds of 5, 10 and 15 use up 100, 200 and 300, and an AMRAP timer is still running after that work is done

themes.theme: Yo-yo intermittent recovery test timer: 20 meters out and back, then 10 seconds to jog

themes.theme: Pyramid interval timer: each rep is a different length, up and then back down
themes.hook: A 1-2-3-4-3-2-1 pyramid changes the work every rep. One work-and-rest pair holds a single length, so the long middle rep never happens

Polar's running journal climbs from 1 minute to 4 and back down, with a jog between each rep. Mile By Mile's time pyramid steps 2, 3 and 4 minutes hard and back down, with one minute easy between. Watta's rower pyramid is 1-2-3-4-3-2-1 minutes and sets the rest equal to the piece just rowed. A timer with one work length and one rest length cannot climb and descend.

On the rower the rest is supposed to match the piece I just finished, and a fixed rest starts the next one early
Halfway through I cannot tell whether I am still going up or already coming down
